transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because of what’s been going on at my apartment. The people there, they watch when I leave and when I come back, and I know they’re putting notes about me to the office. Everyone keeps saying, “No, those are just notices on the doors,” but it’s not like that. I can tell. It’s about me.

And, you know, the office acts like they don’t know, but they always know who’s coming and going… it reminds me of when I used to get in trouble at school for things I didn’t even do. But yeah, that’s why I’m here. I need someone to understand that they’re watching me.
Do you believe that people are talking about you or plotting against you even when there's no clear reason to think so?

Yeah… I do. I mean, it’s not “no reason,” though. At my apartment, they watch when I leave and when I come back, and then those notes show up on the doors, and everybody says, “Oh, that’s just notices,” but I know some of it’s about me going to the office.

It’s like people think I don’t notice things. I’ve always noticed little things, even back when I was younger… teachers would say one thing and then act different later. So, yeah, I know they’re talking about me there, even if nobody wants to admit it.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that others don’t seem to hear?

I don’t know… I mean, sometimes I hear things in the building, like doors or people in the hallway, and it’s hard to tell because these walls are thin. My old place had pipes that made noises all night too, and nobody believed me about that either.

But voices, like… I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I haven’t really sat there and thought, “Only I can hear that.” It’s more that I notice stuff other people don’t pay attention to.
Do you feel like things in other places—like on TV, in newspapers, or in public places—are also secretly about you or sending you messages?

Not really TV or newspapers… I don’t pay much attention to that stuff like some people do. It’s more at my apartment. That’s where it happens.

Like I said, I know the people there are watching when I leave and when I come back, and then these notes get put up, and everybody wants to act like they’re just regular notices on the doors. But I know some of it’s about me, going to the office and all that. They can say it isn’t, but… I’ve been around long enough to know when people are keeping track.
Do you ever feel like things that happen in public, like things people say or events you see, are actually about you even if they don’t seem connected?

It’s not so much, like, out on the street or some big event… I don’t really think about it that way. It’s more where I live. That’s why I came in, because at my apartment I know people are watching when I leave and when I come back, and then those notes show up, and somehow it gets back to the office.

Everybody keeps saying, “No, those are just notices on the doors,” but I don’t buy that. I’ve lived in enough places to know when people are keeping track. Like one time years ago, the landlord would always act surprised when I complained, but then things would change right after, so… yeah, I notice patterns. But public stuff? Not really. It’s the apartment and the office stuff.

Have you ever felt that random events, like something you saw on a billboard, a comment someone made in a store, or something happening in traffic, were actually directed at you or meant something special for you?

Billboards and traffic, no… I don’t really look at those like that. Stores, people say things all the time, half of them don’t even know what they’re talking about.

What I’m saying is, where I live, that’s different. That’s why I came in. I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and when I come back, and then these notes get slipped around or put up, and somehow it all gets back to the office. Everybody keeps telling me, “Oh, those are just notices on the doors,” but I don’t believe that. Not with how it keeps happening.
Have you ever felt that things people say or events that happen in other places — like work, stores, or other buildings — are secretly about you or meant for you, even if they don’t seem connected?

Work and stores… I don’t know, not really like that. I’m not saying every place is doing something.

But the apartment, that’s the thing. That’s why I came in. I know people there are watching when I leave and when I get back, and then these notes show up on the doors, and everybody acts like, “Oh, it’s just notices,” like I’m supposed to believe that. But somehow it always feels like it gets back to the office, like they’re slipping information about me over there.

I’ve dealt with landlords before, you know, and offices always act like they don’t know anything. They say it’s normal paperwork or regular notices, but… I can tell when something’s about me.
Have you ever felt that things people say or events that happen in other places — like work, stores, or other buildings — are secretly about you or meant for you, even if they don’t seem connected?

I mean… other places, I don’t know. I’m not saying the whole world is sending me messages or anything. But at my apartment, that’s where it keeps happening. That’s why I came in.

People there are watching when I leave and when I come back, and then these notes show up on the doors, and everybody says, “Oh, it’s just regular notices,” but it doesn’t feel regular. It’s like they’re keeping track of me and slipping information about me to the office.

And, you know, offices always say they don’t know anything. I’ve dealt with that before. They make it sound like paperwork, but I can tell when something’s about me.
Do you ever feel like people are trying to harm you or are out to get you specifically, beyond what’s happening at your apartment?

Beyond the apartment… I mean, I don’t really go around thinking everybody everywhere is trying to hurt me. It’s not like that.

It’s more where I live. That’s why I came in, because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and when I come back. And then these notes get slipped around or put on the doors, and somehow it gets back to the office. They keep saying it’s just notices, regular notices, but… no, I don’t buy that. Not with the way it keeps happening.
Do you ever feel like you are being watched or followed because you believe you are someone very important or have a special role that others don’t understand?

Important? No, I don’t think it’s because I’m important like on TV or something. I’m not trying to say that.

It’s just… where I live, that apartment building, I came in because I know they watch when I leave and when I come back. And then the notes show up on the doors, and they act like, “Oh, it’s just notices,” but it’s not just that. It gets back to the office somehow. They’re passing things along about me, and everybody keeps acting like I’m supposed to ignore it.
